To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SMC is possible if and only if at least half of the parties are correct and that adding secure hardware to processes improves the efficiency, but not the resilience.

(1) SMC in the new security model is solvable if a majority of participants is correct, (2) this is equivalent to the Uniform Interactive Consistency problem, (3) the complexity of the solutions is polynomial in the number of participants, and (4) the new security model allows to improve the efficiency of SMC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of secure computation among processes with restricted availability.
the following questions: What can be gained by adding secure hardware to secure multi-party computation?
the question whether the addition of secure hardware can improve the resilience and efficiency of secure multi-party protocols.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

SMC can be solved in a model which is more realistic than the standard model but less realistic than a model where processes are equipped with tamper-proof security modules and can be assumed to behave honestly.
the use of secure hardware in secure multi-party computations is not only a good idea but is also necessary.
SMC can be solved efficiently if the number of corrupted processes is small.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the security of the hardware does not increase the security of the software but can improve its performance.
the security of a distributed system can be improved by adding tamper-proof security modules to the processes, while the resilience of the distributed system remains unchanged.
SMC is possible with any number of processes if and only if the number of corrupted parties can be detected by any correct party.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the availability of a security module can be restricted by its host without losing the ability to compute any function in a secure way.
the security of the underlying hardware is a crucial factor for the security of a system.
secure hardware can be a valuable tool in distributed systems.
